content.text: I'll examine the surrounding code to assess structural fit before giving a verdict.

VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED

The new code is mostly well-shaped: the `OwnerHouseholdDuplicateException` + handler pair cleanly mirrors the existing `OwnerIdentityDuplicateException`/handler, `CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique` is a small single-purpose step wired correctly into the pipeline between assign and identity-check, `AssignHousehold` collapses nicely to a one-liner, and the doc updates (including the `OwnerAddress` cleanup that drops the now-false household reference) are thorough. Two structural issues, though:

1. **`OwnerHousehold.of(OwnerFieldsDto)` is now dead code.** This refactor removed the old `household.equals(OwnerHousehold.of(existing))` comparisons; the only remaining caller of the `OwnerHousehold` factory is `AssignHousehold` via `of(owner)` (confirmed by grepping all references — nothing calls the DTO overload). The record is now used purely as a "compute `householdId` from an `Owner`" helper, so the `of(OwnerFieldsDto)` factory should be removed as part of this change rather than left behind. (If anything, the record could be slimmed to just what feeds `householdId()`, since its value-equality semantics are also no longer consumed.)

2. **`CheckPossibleDuplicate` now re-implements "same household" with a different normalization than the single definition it should defer to.** Post-change, a household is keyed on `(lastName, postcode)` in `OwnerHousehold` (last name whitespace-collapsed + lower-cased, postcode stripped). But `CheckPossibleDuplicate` (lines 43-44) still matches the very same "same lastName + postcode" concept inline via `OwnerMatch.equalsIgnoreCase(lastName,…)` + raw `postcode.equals(…)` — i.e. no whitespace collapsing, no postcode strip. These are now two subtly divergent notions of the same thing. The AGENTS/`OwnerHousehold` doc explicitly claims it is "the single definition of 'same household'," yet a maintainer who later tweaks that keying rule (the doc even invites "including city or normalizing the postcode differently") would silently not affect the possible-duplicate flag. Consider expressing the possible-duplicate match in terms of the shared household key (same `householdId`, different telephone) so the definition lives in one place.

Finding 1 is the concrete must-fix; finding 2 is a coherence concern worth addressing while this area is being reworked.
